address: 5646 Milton St. (North Central Expressway), Dallas, TX
recipient: Mr. & Mrs. Felix Yoder, Berne, Ind.
notes: Front caption: “Meadows Building, Dallas, Texas. Located on the North Central Expressway, the Meadows Building is unique in that it has the largest ‘hanging roof garden’ outside Rockefeller Center. The building covers six acres, has parking for 500 cars. Built by the employees of the General American Oil Co. of Texas as a trust for employee pensions. Color by John Messina.” Published by Texas Post Card Co., Dallas / made by Dexter, West Nyack, N.Y. Completed in 1955, the Meadows Building was the first Dallas office tower built outside downtown, designed by architect J.N. MacCammon and named for company president Algur H. Meadows; it was employee-owned through a 1950 pension trust, and its famous hanging garden (by Lambert Landscaping) was removed in 1984 and later restored in a 2020s renovation. 4-cent Lincoln stamp, postmarked Dallas, Tex., 7:30 PM, 30 Nov 1963 — just eight days after President Kennedy's assassination in Dallas on November 22, 1963. Message: “11-30-63. Dear Folks: We got here about 9:00 Thursday morn. OK but tired. It started to rain just before we got to Texas and rained gently the rest of the way. We are seeing the place that saddened the nation. The girls are trying hard to make our stay pleasant. Sam's went on south this morning. Expecting to start for home next Wed morning. Love Dad & Mother” — “the place that saddened the nation” almost certainly refers to Dealey Plaza and the assassination site, making this an ordinary family road-trip card caught up in the immediate aftermath of a defining national tragedy.
feed_description: A Dallas postcard mailed just eight days after JFK's assassination — ‘we are seeing the place that saddened the nation,’ a family writes home from the Meadows Building.
